key_insight: At small batch most MoE experts are cold per token; router-ahead prefetch can hide CXL latency and move expert capacity onto depreciated DDR4.
killer_doubt: At serving batches above ~64 nearly every expert fires each step; a CXL x16 link (~64 GB/s) is ~50-100x below HBM (3-8 TB/s), so offloaded experts stall decode.
decisive_experiment: Replay DeepSeek-V3/Mixtral routing traces at batch 1-256: measure the fraction of experts touched per step and the CXL bytes per step against link bandwidth. Software only, under $20k.
prior_art: Pre-gated MoE (ISCA 2024), MoE-Infinity, Fiddler, KTransformers CPU-DRAM expert offload; Marvell Structera DDR4-reuse CXL controller.

key_insight: For sub-64 B random words (graphs, sparse matrices, small embeddings), memory-side gather-and-pack removes the 80-95% of link bytes that are wasted.
killer_doubt: AI's dominant bytes (weights, 2 KB+ per-token KV, 128-512 B embedding rows) are already 64 B-granular, so the gain is limited to perhaps <10% of HBM traffic.
decisive_experiment: Profile LLM decode, DLRM and GNN traces for the share of 64 B lines with <25% useful bytes. If it is under 10% of bytes, stop; otherwise model a base-die gather unit in Ramulator. Under $50k.
prior_art: Impulse memory controller (Utah, 1999), GS-DRAM (MICRO 2015), RecNMP (ISCA 2020), Samsung AxDIMM embedding lookup in the buffer chip.

key_insight: Top-k attention lets memory return ~5-10% of KV. Done where internal bandwidth exceeds the link, long-context KV can live in cheaper DRAM, not HBM.
killer_doubt: The HBM base die sees only TSV bandwidth (about the ~2 TB/s PHY), so base-die scoring saves only PHY energy (~20-30% of 3-4 pJ/bit). In-bank scoring is the real lever.
decisive_experiment: In Ramulator2+DRAMPower, compare base-die and in-bank MSB-plane-sketch scoring against Quest on unmodified HBM, on RULER-128k: tokens/s, pJ/token and accuracy at k=2-10%. Under $150k.
prior_art: Quest (ICML 2024), InfiniGen (OSDI 2024), AttAcc (ASPLOS 2024), H2EAL (2025 preprint), IBM StarC; Phase B N-70; R11 I-09070.

key_insight: Read-only weights need O(1) copies. A passive splitter tree can feed many decode-only replicas in lockstep, leaving each accelerator's HBM for KV.
killer_doubt: Each leaf must ingest weights at HBM rate (~2-8 TB/s, while NICs give ~0.1 TB/s). Rack-scale sharding already keeps weights at only ~5-10% of an NVL72's ~20 TB of HBM.
decisive_experiment: Fleet model of HBM freed versus replica size (HGX-8 to NVL72) and model size. Plus an FPGA bench: a 1:32 splitter, 100G PAM4 lanes, two boards decoding a small model in lockstep; measure BER and utilization. ~$300k.
prior_art: Fiber Memory preprint (arXiv 2607.08407): splitter-tapped fiber weight broadcast to pods (via search snippet); Cerebras MemoryX/SwarmX weight streaming; Phase B N-80.

key_insight: The same O(1)-weights insight as I-05406, using mass-produced telecom PON splitters as a cheap broadcast medium.
killer_doubt: PON optics carry 10-50 Gb/s per wavelength. One accelerator's weight reads (~2 TB/s, ~16 Tb/s) need ~300-1,600 PON lanes per leaf. It duplicates I-05406.
decisive_experiment: No separate test: fold it into I-05406's link-budget bench. A desk check of whether any PON-class part reaches >=400 Gb/s per fiber through a 1:16 split within budget. Under $10k.
prior_art: Same as I-05406: Fiber Memory preprint (arXiv 2607.08407), Cerebras SwarmX weight broadcast; Phase B N-80.

key_insight: Glass panels cost ~200x less per m2 than finished DRAM wafers (~$61k/m2), and memory in the package substrate sits millimetres under the chiplets.
killer_doubt: A 2T oxide gain cell at 45 nm half-pitch is ~0.07 um2 (~1/30 of 1-beta density), which cancels the area-cost gap. No NIL tool overlays ~8 nm across Gen-8 glass.
decisive_experiment: A desk cost model of a 6-8-layer oxide gain-cell flow on Gen-2/3.5 glass with step-and-repeat NIL. Then imprint two aligned layers on 300 mm glass at a university fab and measure overlay. ~$200k.
prior_art: SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; Intel glass-core substrates; Canon NIL trials at Kioxia; J-FIL wire-grid polarizers on glass; Phase B N-36, N-50.

key_insight: Lockstep predictors at both ends of a link send only residuals, so zero-, pointer- and stride-heavy CPU traffic compresses with no metadata.
killer_doubt: AI tensors dominate memory bytes and are nearly incompressible (FP8 weights ~1.1-1.3x). Published value-locality link compression gets ~1.3-2x, not 2-5x, and DRAM dies have no predictor logic.
decisive_experiment: Replay memory-link traces (SPEC, graph, LLM decode) through stride, context and FCM predictors in software, and measure bits per transferred line. If AI traffic compresses under 1.3x, stop. Under $20k.
prior_art: Thuresson et al., value-locality memory-link compression (IEEE TC 2008); frequent-value bus encoding; toggle-aware compression (HPCA 2016).

key_insight: Bonded links are kT/C-limited at ~0.2 mV rms on 100 fF, so sense-amp-style precharge, share and regenerate signalling could run at 20 mV swing.
killer_doubt: I/O swing is ~15-25% of HBM's 3-4 pJ/bit; activation and datapaths dominate. NVIDIA GRS already reached 0.54 pJ/b; full-swing CV2 on a 50 fF bond is ~0.03 pJ.
decisive_experiment: A 28 nm MPW: 64 lanes over a 2 mm interposer-like line, with a 20 mV charge-dump TX and a trimmed StrongARM RX. Measure BER at 4-8 Gb/s, crosstalk, supply-noise margin and fJ/bit. ~$150k.
prior_art: Ho/Horowitz low-swing on-chip wires; NVIDIA ground-referenced signalling (0.54 pJ/b, 2013); capacitively coupled low-swing links; StrongARM latch receivers.

key_insight: Placing bit-planes across dies by significance gives AI stacks a use for refresh-relaxed, low-voltage or reject dies, and allows precision-on-demand fetches.
killer_doubt: With FP8/FP4 only ~25% of bits sit in tolerant low-order planes, not two-thirds, and refresh is ~5-10% of active HBM power. Sparkk did cross-chip significance placement in 2014.
decisive_experiment: Inject LSB-plane errors (1e-4 to 1e-2 BER, plus row/column fault maps from a few hundred real reject dies) into FP8/BF16 LLM weights and KV, and measure perplexity. ~$80k.
prior_art: Sparkk (2014) per-chip significance-aware refresh; Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); EDEN approximate DRAM (MICRO 2019); Phase B N-77 bit-plane memory.

key_insight: Retention is a spec, not physics: if streaming restores every row every ~100 us, the capacitor and leakage requirements relax ~640x.
killer_doubt: A 28-40 nm planar-MIM cell is ~0.05-0.1 um2, 50-100x 1-beta's ~0.001 um2, and depreciated wafers are only ~2x cheaper, so cost/bit is ~25-50x worse. Circulating also costs ~1 W/GB.
decisive_experiment: A desk check of cell area and wafer cost at 28/40 nm against 1-beta, plus circulation power at 10-100 fJ/bit per restore. If cost/bit is above 1-beta, stop. Under $10k.
prior_art: Gain-cell eDRAM with microsecond retention (Teman, Giterman); Smart Refresh (MICRO 2007), where access acts as refresh; delay-line memory; Fiber Memory preprint (arXiv 2607.08407).

key_insight: Bonding the array wafer to a logic wafer moves the ~49% periphery off the DRAM die and exposes per-mat parallelism: array efficiency ~0.51 to ~0.75, and far more bandwidth.
killer_doubt: Already shipping: UniIC SeDRAM bonds DRAM to logic wafers (34 GB/s/Gb, 0.88 pJ/b; two SoCs in mass production). Samsung PUC is on incumbents' roadmaps. Needs a DRAM line.
decisive_experiment: Nothing a $1M team can settle. For the venture, model array efficiency and $/bit including the cost of the bonded logic wafer, using SeDRAM-reported data. Under $30k.
prior_art: UniIC SeDRAM on XMC 3DLink (via search snippet); Tezzaron DiRAM; Samsung periphery-under-cell for 4F2; YMTC Xtacking and Kioxia CBA in NAND.

key_insight: Micro-transfer printing plus lithographic vias gives bump-free 2-3 um-pitch memory-on-logic with university tools, a prototyping route around wafer-to-wafer hybrid-bonding capital.
killer_doubt: Hybrid bonding already runs <=10 um pitch in production (SoIC, SeDRAM). ~1-2 um print placement error forces per-die adaptive patterning; bought DRAM dies expose only ~100s of pads.
decisive_experiment: Print ten thinned (<10 um) test chiplets onto a patterned wafer, planarize with BCB and pattern 2.5 um-pitch vias with per-die alignment. Measure via yield, resistance and thermal-cycle survival. ~$150k at a university fab.
prior_art: X-Celeprint/Rogers micro-transfer printing of CMOS chiplets; Deca adaptive patterning; chip-first fan-out (InFO); imec micro-transfer printing of III-V on silicon photonics.
